issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a no-argument method getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int, and the template TODO refers to that method name, but the solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests). This parameter mismatch changes the required signature and behavior, which will confuse students about which method to implement and prevents direct conformance to the specification/tests that expect a no-arg method.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the specification by providing a no-argument getTotalNumberOfStudents() method returning int (e.g., summing inscribed and guest students), and optionally overload with getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean) if desired. Alternatively, update the problem statement and template to require the boolean parameter, but keep all three artifacts consistent.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a method getTotalNumberOfStudents() with no parameters, but the solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests). This introduces a different API (an extra parameter identifier 'includeGuests') for the same conceptual operation, breaking the expected mapping between the exercise description/tests and the implementation. Students will be confused about which method signature to implement and how to call it from other methods (e.g., getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor) or tests that expect a no-argument method.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the API with the problem statement and UML by providing a no-argument method getTotalNumberOfStudents() that returns the total number of students (inscribed + guest). If the boolean behavior is desired, add an overloaded method getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests) but keep the no-arg getTotalNumberOfStudents() to match the exercise description and tests.
